description:
⚠️ **CHECK CIDOC-CRM BEFORE AUTHORING (2026-08-13 portfolio scan).** This tasklist extends a canonical schema, and the scan found that **CIDOC-CRM** — the ISO-standard cultural-heritage semantic model, whose classes are Person / Place / Event / Type — is the established ontology for exactly the shape pinakes holds, and is not mentioned anywhere in pinakes's tasklists. The same scan confirmed Wikibase as the standard substrate (FactGrid for historical research, Lingua Libre, enslaved.org, Qichwabase all run domain Wikibases), which validates D4(b) — so the substrate call is right and only the ONTOLOGY question is open. **Authoring a canonical schema without first checking whether a standard one exists is the exact failure the portfolio review was created to catch.** The honest counter-argument, to be tested rather than assumed: CIDOC-CRM is built for cultural-heritage objects and events, and a linguistic/genetic correspondence graph may not fit it — a forced fit is worse than a fitted schema of your own.

---

Canonical-schema extension for learned inference (COVERAGE-AUDIT N9). lugh's 210-scallop-virtuous-loop-writeback feeds the trained Scallop edge-scorer's probabilities back onto `inferred:` edges and is contract-bound to PROPOSE the schema change upstream to pinakes rather than fork it — its writeback dead-ends until pinakes lands (1) a LEARNED-PROBABILITY edge attribute (a soft, model-produced probability, deliberately distinct from the curated `confidence` column and the confidence-rubric priors) and (2) a REASONING-SCOPE marker recording which reasoning scope/run produced the value, so consistency/tier evaluators can read learned confidences without confusing them with curated ones. NAMING REALITY: lugh 210 and insimul 210 both call this 'canonical schema v1.2', a label coined before pinakes's contracts/canonical-schema.json reached its current version 1.3.0 — land the change as the NEXT version bump from the version on disk and record the 'v1.2' alias in the changelog/doc so the cross-repo references resolve. Deliverables: the contract JSON edit + `bun run gen:contracts` regeneration (never hand-edit generated bindings), docs/canonical-schema.md, and validator/export acceptance of the new columns. Downstream (out of scope, named): lugh re-vendors its byte-mirror after this lands. D4(b) NOTE (docs/DECISION-D4-CLDF-AND-WIKIBASE.md §5): under the Wikibase model these two attributes are naturally a statement QUALIFIER (the learned probability) and a REFERENCE/scope marker (the reasoning run) rather than edge columns — 121's property ontology must give both a home, and the mapping validator there will fail if it does not. That does NOT defer this tasklist: the columns are the transitional carrier lugh 210 is blocked on today, and the migration is a 2-3 month program (120-124) that lugh cannot wait on.

userStories.title: Does a standard ontology already model this?
userStories.description: Added by the 2026-08-13 scan. Answer before extending the schema, since the answer changes what gets authored.
acceptanceCriteria: CIDOC-CRM is assessed against pinakes's canonical entity/edge model, naming which of its concepts map cleanly, which do not, and which pinakes needs that it does not express.

The `inferred:` edges with learned probabilities that this tasklist exists to carry are checked specifically — a probabilistic edge is where a heritage ontology is most likely NOT to fit, and that is the load-bearing case.

The verdict is one of ADOPT / PROFILE-OVER (a constrained profile of the standard, koine's own posture toward its ~60% profiles-over-standards) / DECLINE, recorded with evidence so the question closes.
If DECLINE, the reason is written where a future audit will find it, so the standard is not re-proposed at every scan.

userStories.title: Schema + contracts codegen for learned probability and reasoning scope
userStories.description: Add the learned-probability edge attribute and the reasoning-scope marker to the canonical schema contract, bump the version, and regenerate both bindings.
acceptanceCriteria: contracts/canonical-schema.json gains a learned-probability edge attribute (soft probability in [0,1], explicitly distinct from the curated `confidence` provenance column — the doc states which evaluators read which) and a reasoning-scope marker (identifying the reasoning scope/run that produced the value), with the version bumped from the on-disk 1.3.0 and the historical cross-repo 'v1.2' label recorded as an alias in docs/canonical-schema.md.

`bun run gen:contracts` regenerates the TS + Python bindings from the JSON source (both committed; nothing under contracts/generated/ or contracts/python/ hand-edited) and `bun run check:contracts` passes.
`bun run check`, `bun run test`, and `.chief/verify.sh` pass; the contract JSON parses.

userStories.title: Validators and the export/QA path accept the new columns
userStories.description: The engine's schema validators, headers, and the convergence-QA drift gate accept (and correctly type) the new edge columns so a writeback carrying them round-trips instead of being rejected or silently dropped.
acceptanceCriteria: The engine-side schema surfaces (pinakes_engine schema/headers + Datalog schema constraints, which parse the contract's own cells) accept edges carrying the learned-probability attribute + reasoning-scope marker, validate the probability range, and never conflate the value with curated `confidence`; tests cover an edge with and without the new columns.

The convergence-QA drift gate and the export/write-back path tolerate the new optional columns (no false 'unmapped column' drift, no writeback of graph-owned learned values into curated lexicons — the new columns join the non-writeback set), covered by a test.

The applicable gates pass: `uv run --all-packages pytest -q engine/tests`, `uv run ruff check .` + `uv run mypy src` (engine), and `.chief/verify.sh`; the change is documented as the upstream landing lugh 210's dependsOn waits on.
